name: vLLM
summary: vLLM is an open-source inference engine for serving LLMs on your own GPUs. It uses PagedAttention memory management, continuous batching and prefix caching to raise throughput, and ships an OpenAI-compatible server that also speaks the Anthropic Messages API. It started at UC Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab and is maintained by a broad community.
facts: UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab; 2,000+ contributors
OpenAI-compatible server, Anthropic Messages API, gRPC
NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs, CPUs; plugins for TPU, Gaudi, Ascend, Apple Silicon
PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill, prefix caching, quantization
goodFor: High-concurrency serving of open models on your GPUs
Keeping model traffic inside your own infrastructure
Day-0 support for new open-weight releases
watchOut: Needs GPUs and ops skills to run well
Serves models you host; does not route to hosted APIs
